intro: Explicit bucket boundaries turn raw quantities into a stable reporting schema. Keeping empty bins means reports remain comparable even when some ranges have no observations.
task: Bucket nonnegative integer quantities by explicit increasing upper bounds.
requirements: values are integers 0..1e9. upper_bounds are strictly increasing integers 0..1e9. Return len(bounds)+1 counts: each value goes to the first bound >= value, or the final overflow bin.
Sequence inputs are Python lists or tuples of at most 1000 items. Integer inputs must be Python ints, excluding bool, within the task-specific bounds or -1e9..1e9 when no narrower bounds are stated.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Advance past a bound only when the value is strictly greater than it.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Always allocate the overflow bin, even if all observed values fit earlier bins.

explanation: Explicit bucket boundaries turn raw quantities into a stable reporting schema. Keeping empty bins means reports remain comparable even when some ranges have no observations.
Boundary equality belongs to the lower indexed bucket under this contract. A conservation check is that the sum of counts equals the number of input values.
